questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always been fascinated about USA and I wanted to experience it in person. The US college is quite different than European ones, I'm really glad I got to study there for semester abroad.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, USF offered exchange meetings where all the exchange participants got all the necessary information. Contact with exchange coordinator Lauren Strange was also supreme.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: With the help of Lauren Strange we manage to fulfill my exchange courses requirement and found best study path for me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I could chose from 3 different types of dormitories, traditional style, suite style and apartment style.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: USF campus provided full dining option for extra charge, it was either unlimited or limited packages

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I went for apartment style dorm to have bigger comfort, same goes with unlimited meal plan, but after all I didn't use meal plan that much due to traveling and all other food options available on campus, so I would suggest to go for 60 meal plan or higher but not necessarily for unlimited and as for the housing I would suggest to go for traditional dorm style, because its a great opportunity to make life-lasting international friendships, while apartment style with own room in 4 room apartment gives more privacy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After arrival we had less than a week to fulfill visa requirements and pick our classes, not all classes were offered and some needed prerequisite courses, which might lead to the need to change our initial preapproval for courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Exchange coordinator Lauren Strange made sure we all fulfill the visa requirements on time and took great care of this process, providing assistance and guidance in case of any doubt or troubles while registering.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't meet all the requirements for all the courses I wanted and some of them were not offered. My course IT&Cognition had quite specific main subject which was little hard to replace but at the end Lauran and I found a solution that was accepted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare some backup courses and prepare for the need to pick a new one if the course wont be offered, but there's nothing to stress about the process it quite simple and USF exchange coordinators provide all the necessary help needed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found my courses relevant to the courses I take at UCPH. Hopefully I can use the gathered knowledge during writing my masters thesis.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: US academic approach differs from the one offered at UCPH, which means UCPH approach is more interpersonal, while USF provides more guidance and weekly assignments and various methods to check if the student actually prepares for the class. It was really exciting to experience how it looks like to study in America and I think it definitely broadens my horizons and keep me prepared in my academic field.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Global Cyber Ethics, Business Intelligence, Python for business analytics and Intro to psychological science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found Intro to psychological science the most exciting and relevant to my course cognitive science. It let me have a look on broader perspective of the psychology aspect.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It's hard to move around Tampa without own transportation, the public transport doesn't really exist if we want to go to city center or to the beach, uber and lyft were the transportation we had to use, or carpool with our american friends

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: books are quite expensive depending on subject it can cost up to 1050 dkk for a single coursebook

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Swimming, basketball, football, soccer, bike club, martial arts and many more, USF really have a lot of sport clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Bike club was really fun, they make long trips and weekly training sessions.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: For someone who never visited USA I definitely recommend seeing NY its worth it, and Miami as well. During fall exchange it is interesting to experience Thanksgiving. Americans are very welcoming, so after you make some friends there is a high chance they will invite you to celebrate with them since they know we don't celebrate it or have anyone to celebrate with since our families are bk home.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I adjusted quite fast, some Americans had a tough accent, but I got used to it pretty fast.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join some sport clubs it's really worth it.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The way of contacting your professors must stay very formal.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The attitude fo Americans towards exchnage students, families were very welcoming and invited use to see how they celebrate American holidays such as thanksgiving.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't stress and have fun, it's a lifetime opportunity to study at US campus. Take your time to really explore it and take the most of your time there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plan your trip wisely USA is huge and it can be too expensive to see everything.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to experience. the way of American lifestyle as college student

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Meet the deadlines of the assignments, especially if you go for weekend escapes to travel around the country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
